How to Transform Leftover Custard Into a Seasonal Fruit Fool

30 Oct 2026, 11:22 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Lifestyle Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

2 min read

Key takeawaysLeftover custard from holiday baking or previous meals often sits forgotten in the refrigerator, but a simple zero-waste recipe offers a practical way to turn those remnants into a traditional British dessert. A Zero-Waste Approach to a Classic Dessert

Leftover custard from holiday baking or previous meals often sits forgotten in the refrigerator, but a simple zero-waste recipe offers a practical way to turn those remnants into a traditional British dessert. By combining leftover custard or yogurt with whipped cream and seasonal fruit, home cooks can prepare a traditional fool with minimal effort.

Traditional versions often feature gooseberries, rhubarb, or strawberries, but the recipe adapts easily to what is currently available in local markets or refrigerators. Autumn variations make good use of seasonal produce such as blackberries and apples.

Recipe and Preparation Details

The preparation focuses on reducing food waste by utilizing ingredients on hand. For an apple and blackberry variation, finely dicing the apple allows the skin to remain on, which preserves fiber and adds texture while saving preparation time.

Ingredients:

  • 100g blackberries, plus extra for garnish
  • 1 apple, finely diced
  • ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
  • ¼ tsp ginger (ground or freshly grated)
  • A pinch of sea salt
  • 3 tbsp honey
  • 100ml double cream, chilled
  • 150ml custard, yogurt, or a mix of both

To cook the fruit, combine the blackberries, diced apple, cinnamon, ginger, sea salt, and a splash of water in a small saucepan. Simmer covered for approximately 10 minutes until the fruit softens, mash with a fork, stir in the honey after cooling, and refrigerate.

For the dairy base, whip the chilled double cream to soft peaks. Gently fold in the custard using a metal spoon, followed by two-thirds of the chilled fruit puree to create a rippled effect. Spoon the mixture into glasses and top with the remaining puree and fresh blackberries.
